cards.definition: The branch of medicine that deals with the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of tumors and cancer.
A disease characterized by the uncontrolled growth and spread of abnormal cells.
A non-cancerous growth that does not spread to other parts of the body and is usually not life-threatening.
A cancerous growth that can invade nearby tissues and spread (metastasize) to other parts of the body.
The spread of cancer cells from the primary tumor to distant parts of the body.
The removal of a small sample of cells or tissue for examination under a microscope to diagnose disease.
A series of tests (lab, imaging, etc.) to detect cancer and assess its extent.
Treatment aimed at completely eradicating cancer and achieving a long-term cure. Also known as Definitive Treatment.
Treatment focused on relieving symptoms and improving quality of life when a cure is not possible.
The main treatment administered for the best chance of curing the cancer or controlling its growth.
Administering two or more types of treatment at the same time (e.g., radiation and chemotherapy).
Additional treatment given *after* the primary treatment to eliminate any remaining cancer cells and reduce recurrence risk.
Treatment given *before* the primary treatment, often to shrink a tumor.
A treatment modality involving the physical removal of tumors or cancerous tissue.
Treatment using drugs to kill cancer cells; typically a systemic treatment.
Treatment using high-energy radiation to shrink tumors and kill cancer cells; typically a localized treatment.
